prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, demi-statue demi statue portrait, a 6-cell grid body (3 rows, two columns), every cell a genuinely different material, every seam physically stepped, no bare skin below the collarbones. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to two individually finished thigh tips a little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her form comes to an end, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult American woman in Instagram glam makeup — sun-kissed skin, heavily sculpted contour and a strong highlighter on the cheekbones, bold defined brows, long fluffy false lashes, shimmery bronze eyeshadow, large eyes with bright real catchlights, plump glossy nude lips with a defined lip-liner outline, long voluminous honey-blonde waves, a confident, camera-ready smile. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. Two big gold hoops stacked on each ear.

Physique: A giant hourglass frame flaring at both ends — shoulders more than four times a normal woman's width, a colossal chest projecting past them, a big round belly, no waist at all, hips as broad as the shoulders, body divided into a 6-cell grid (3 rows, two columns), each cell a different material, stepped seams.

Boundary: a single straight, flat line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones, never jagged, never zigzag — real skin above, material immediately below, no skin anywhere lower. At that line, the material's edge rises in a small raised step, casting a crisp shadow.

Below the collarbones, her body is divided into a grid of 6 cells — 3 horizontal rows crossed by one vertical centre line — each cell with a raised stepped edge and shadow at every border, no gaps, no skin anywhere. Row 1 (her whole left arm and left chest / her whole right arm and right chest): left cell carved solid richly streaked cream, rose-pink and violet Brazilian tulipwood, completely opaque; right cell carved solid deep black ebony with fine dense grain, completely opaque. Row 2 (left / right body band 2): left cell carved solid deep reddish-brown rosewood streaked with black, completely opaque; right cell clear turquoise water with drifting bubbles. Row 3 (left thigh-stub tip / right thigh-stub tip (a little further below the middle of her thighs, just above where the knee would be)): left cell clear rose-pink water with drifting rose petals, sealing shut at its tip; right cell clear sapphire-blue water with drifting stars, sealing shut at its tip.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a soft periwinkle blue on one side and a warm champagne gold on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: standing tall, her left hand resting on her flared hip, her right arm held clear of her body, the hand relaxed at hip height, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: two large softboxes rake across her body from either side, so blue light glances off one side and gold light glances off the other, catching a crisp glint along every stepped seam in the grid. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
